description: Default capability for the main window. Filesystem access is the app's own data plus the folders the user picked (DEL-89, fs-scope-plan). Static scope: $APPDATA/stores (the durable stores, M1) read-write, and $CONFIG/ohhi (the user resource root: layouts, keymaps, templates; ~/.config/ohhi on Linux) read-only through command scopes on exists, read-dir and read-text-file only. Nothing under $HOME. A vault folder enters the scope when the user picks it: the dialog plugin's open() with recursive: true grants it at runtime, tauri-plugin-persisted-scope saves the grant in Rust and restores it on the next launch, and src/lib.rs (granted_folders) mirrors each grant into a runtime capability so its dot-entries (.ohhi/, .obsidian/) match too (plugins.fs.requireLiteralLeadingDot is false in tauri.conf.json). The writing harness's <vault>/.agents/ (skills, writing-harness-shaping B9) and <vault>/.claude/ (the skills farm the app copies for Claude Code) are dot-entries of the granted folder the same way, so they need no entry of their own. Dropping a file or folder on the window grants it the same way (the fs plugin's own behaviour). The grant file, $APPDATA/.persisted-scope, is denied to the webview here as well as by the plugin, so a script in the webview cannot grant itself more on the next launch. Updater: check, download and install (not the download-and-install shortcut), plus process:allow-restart to relaunch into an installed update. Guide windows (first-run E4): core:webview:allow-create-webview-window lets this window open the Help menu's bundled guide pages in a second window, and core:window:allow-set-focus brings an already-open guide window forward; that window is in no capability, so it gets no IPC (docs/desktop-builds.md, Guide windows). The feed URL and signing key live in tauri.conf.json, so the webview can neither repoint the updater nor make it accept an unsigned build.
